Modern payment systems now use chip-and-PIN or EMV cards, which encrypt the data on the chip itself. This means that even if the magnetic stripe is compromised, the data remains unreadable without the correct cryptographic key. For academic work, you can find detailed specifications on how these encryption standards evolved over time, but the underlying physical vulnerability remains a key factor in why they were phased out.
